summary: Monthly company all-hands. CEO update on milestones and hiring, CTO update on reliability and Dedicated product, Product update on roadmap (Optimize + Private deployments), brief Q&A, and org announcements. Several references to last week's outage and action items to address reliability and communication.
transcript:
[00:00] Nadia Gupta: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick mic check.. okay great. Welcome to the July all hands. we'll run about an hour, try to keep time for questions at the end. Um, so first up, a quick wins and then the org updates.
[00:17] Michael Lee: Good morning, afternoon, whatever timezone you're in. I'll start with reliability notes. As you all know we had a partial outage last Thursday that impacted hosted API requests for about 45 minutes, due to a autoscaler bug interacting with the new batching service. Jordan and infra team have been chipping away on it.
[00:36] Jordan Kim: yeah so the short version is autoscaler metrics were reading an aggregate with a skewed window, and the scale down triggered before in-flight batches drained. that produced a transient cache invalidation and higher latencies. we're shipping a fix to the scaler and adding a safety valve to prevent scale-down during active batching windows.
[00:55] Jordan Kim: the postmortem is on the wiki, link in the chat (internal link). we'll also do an all-hands follow-up for SRE and infra folks to review lessons learned.
[01:12] Nadia Gupta: Thanks Jordan. I want to emphasize how the team responded — incident response was fast and customers appreciated proactive comms, but we need to reduce MTTR and eliminate the root cause. We'll prioritize tests in the CI that emulate continuous batching scenarios.
[01:30] Priya Patel: On product, we shipped the Optimize beta to 20 customers last month; early signals look promising — average token spend down ~18% for inference-heavy workloads when customers applied suggested batching + cache settings. There's still improvement work around suggestions for embeddings-heavy flows.
[01:50] Priya Patel: Private deployments: three pilots live this quarter, two in EMEA, one on-prem for a regulated customer. We're learning a lot about install automation and KMS integrations. Expect hardened installer v1 in Q3.
[02:10] Michael Lee: A quick note on Dedicated: our Dedicated offering is hitting the right pockets of demand — customers who need predictable throughput and SLOs. We're improving autoscale semantics for reserved pools so you get the best of both worlds: predictable capacity and burstable headroom.
[02:30] Speaker 1: (whisper) congrats team — nice work on Dedicated.
[02:36] Maya Ortiz: People & hiring — we're rephasing the hiring plan to slow down non-critical individual contributor hiring and accelerate SRE and Platform roles given the reliability priorities. We also have some leadership changes: Clara Wang is moving from Solutions Eng to Head of Customer Reliability, starting 2026-07-20. Please congratulate Clara.
[02:58] Nadia Gupta: thanks Maya. A note on metrics: revenue growth is on track vs plan, net dollar retention looks solid. I want to highlight a few enterprise deals we closed this quarter, notably a mid-market fintech with on-prem requirements — big win for Private.
[03:20] Nadia Gupta: We also need to be mindful of margins: as we grow Dedicated and Private, unit economics matter so Optimize recommendations and model quantization will be important levers.
[03:34] Audience Q: (raised hand) question about SOC 2 and certifications — are we on track for the next audit?
[03:41] Michael Lee: Yes, SOC 2 readiness is progressing. We completed the control mapping and remediation plan; external audit is scheduled for late Q3. We are also evaluating ISO 27001 as a follow-up next year.
[03:56] Audience Q: any changes to data retention and audit logs for Private customers?
[04:02] Priya Patel: For Private, customers can choose audit retention windows and we support KMS/HSM integrations. we're adding more granular token-level logging options in the console, and soon a compliance package add-on.
[04:18] Nadia Gupta: Marketing & GTM — sales plays are updated to emphasize cost/perf benchmarking with real customer workloads; we have new case studies (internal doc links) that reps can use. Also pushing more content around migration from other hosted vendors.
[04:35] Speaker 2: Quick plug — the benchmarks deck is up in the sales repo. Please don't share externally until marketing finalizes the blinding pass.
[04:45] Nadia Gupta: Alright let's take a few questions from the chat, and then we'll wrap.
[04:50] [Q&A segment — selected questions pulled from chat]
[04:51] Employee A: Will there be more transparency on pricing for Dedicated?
[04:54] Priya Patel: Yes, Sales + Product are aligning on a simplified pricing sheet for Dedicated that will show typical throughput/price bands and recommended configs. expect a draft next week.
[05:06] Employee B: For the outage, are customers who saw errors getting credits?
[05:09] Jordan Kim: we're evaluating case-by-case with CS, and sending proactive credits where appropriate. incident blameless review will guide the approach.
[05:19] Employee C: Any updates on SDKs/streaming improvements?
[05:22] Michael Lee: streaming is getting lower-latency patches; SDK teams are rolling them out gradually. We'll also add more robust retries for flaky networks.
[05:33] Nadia Gupta: quick recap: 1) reliability work is top priority, follow-ups from SRE/infra, 2) folks to review Dedicated rollout plan, 3) hiring shift to prioritize SRE & Platform, 4) Clara's move and org updates.
[05:47] Nadia Gupta: Next steps — execs will share Q3 priorities doc by Friday, and Product will share rollout plan for Dedicated with Sales. If you have questions, ping execs or join the product open office hours next Tuesday.
[05:58] Michael Lee: Thanks everyone, and huge thanks to on-call and incident responders.
[06:02] [meeting ends]

Note: transcript contains occasional transcription artifacts from the automatic recorder (names/terms like KV cache sometimes spelled as K-V cache; 'autoscaler' sometimes appears as 'auto scaler'). References to docs and decks were posted in the meeting chat as internal links.
